bibl.title: A potter’s way of bookkeeping. A tally stick from early Islamic Egypt
bibl.seg: Gesa Schenke, A Potter's Way of Bookkeeping. A Tally Stick from Early Islamic Egypt.

Nathalie Bosson, Anne Boud'hors & Sydney H. Aufrère (edd.), Labor omnia uicit improbus. Miscellanea in honorem Ariel Shisha-Halevy = Orientalia Lovaniensia Analecta. 256 (Leuven - Paris - Bristol, 2017) pp. 349-354, figg.
bibl.note: Edition of an inscribed potter's reed. It seems to have functioned as a tally stick, a mnemonic device recording quantities of goods, which could function as a legal document when presented as a record for compensation.
